source_text:
Ἀβραάμ, ὁ φίλος προσαγορευθείς, πιστὸς εὑρέθη ἐν τῷ αὐτὸν ὑπήκοον γενέσθαι τοῖς ῥήμασιν τοῦ θεοῦ.
οὗτος δἰ ὑπακοῆς ἐξῆλθεν ἐκ τῆς γῆς αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐκ τῆς συγγενείας αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐκ τοῦ οἴκου τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ, ὅπως γῆν ὀλίγην καὶ συγγένειαν ἀσθενῆ καὶ οἶκον μικρὸν καταλιπὼν κληρονομήσῃ τὰς ἐπαγγελίας τοῦ θεοῦ. λέγει γὰρ αὐτῷ:
Ἄπελθε ἐκ τῆς γῆς σου καὶ ἐκ τῆς συγγενείας σου καὶ ἐκ τοῦ οἴκου τοῦ πατρός σου εἰς τὴν γῆν ἣν ἄν σοι δείξω: καὶ ποιήσω σε εἰς ἔθνος μέγα καὶ εὐλογήσω σε καὶ μεγαλυνῶ τὸ ὄνομά σου, καὶ ἔσῃ εὐλογημένος: καὶ εὐλογήσω τοὺς εὐλογοῦντάς σε καὶ καταράσομαι τοὺς καταρωμένους σε, καὶ εὐλογηθήσονται ἐν σοὶ πᾶσαι αἱ φυλαὶ τῆς γῆς.
καὶ πάλιν ἐν τῷ διαχωρισθῆναι αὐτὸν ἀπὸ Λὼτ εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ θεός. Ἀναβλέψας τοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς σου ἴδε ἀπὸ τοῦ τόπου, οὖ νῦν σὺ εἶ, πρὸς βορρᾶν καὶ λίβα καὶ ἀνατολὰς καὶ θάλασσαν, ὅτι πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν, ἣν σὺ ὁρᾷς, σοὶ δώσω αὐτὴν καὶ τῷ σπέρματί σου ἕως αἰῶνος.
καὶ ποιήσω τὸ σπέρμα σου ὡς τὴν ἄμμον τῆς γῆς: εἰ δύναταί τις ἐξαριθμῆσαι τὴν ἄμμον τῆς γῆς, καὶ τὸ σπέρμα σου ἐξαριθμηθήσεται.
καὶ πάλιν λέγει: Ἐξήγαγεν ὁ θεὸς τὸν Ἀβραὰμ καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ: Ἀνάβλεψον εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ ἀρίθμησον τοὺς ἀστέρας, εἰ δυνήσῃ ἐξαριθμῆσαι αὐτούς: οὕτως ἔσται τὸ σπέρμα σου. ἐπίστευσεν δὲ Ἀβραὰμ τῷ θεῷ, καὶ ἐλογίσθη αὐτῷ εἰς δικαιοσύνην.
διὰ πίστιν καὶ φιλοξενίαν ἐδόθη αὐτῷ υἱὸς ἐν γήρᾳ, καὶ δἰ ὑπακοῆς προσήνεγκεν αὐτὸν θυσίαν τῷ θεῷ πρὸς τὸ ὄρος ὃ ἔδειξεν αὐτῷ.
orientation: The Roman church continues its list of ancient examples of obedience, now turning to Abraham, whom God called out of his homeland and blessed with promises.
pass_a_gloss: Abraham, the friend [who was] addressed [as such], was found faithful in his becoming obedient to the words of God. This [man] through obedience went out from his land and from his kindred and from the house of his father, so that, having left behind a small land and a weak kindred and a little house, he might inherit the promises of God. For he says to him: 'Go out from your land and from your kindred and from the house of your father into the land which I will show you: and I will make you into a great nation and I will bless you and I will magnify your name, and you will be blessed: and I will bless those who bless you and I will curse those who curse you, and in you all the tribes of the earth will be blessed.' And again, when he was separated from Lot, God said to him: 'Having looked up with your eyes, see from the place where you now are, toward the north and the south and the east and the sea, that all the land which you see, I will give it to you and to your seed forever. And I will make your seed as the sand of the earth: if anyone is able to count the sand of the earth, then your seed will be counted.' And again he says: 'God brought Abraham out and said to him: Look up into the heaven and count the stars, if you are able to count them: so will your seed be.' And Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned to him for righteousness. Through faith and hospitality a son was given to him in old age, and through obedience he offered him as a sacrifice to God at the mountain which he showed him.

choices.why: Keeps the passive participle force of προσαγορευθείς (having been addressed/called) rather than turning it into a simple title

choices.term: γῆν ὀλίγην καὶ συγγένειαν ἀσθενῆ καὶ οἶκον μικρὸν
choices.english: a small land and a weak kindred and a little house
choices.why: Preserves the threefold contrast of adjectives (small, weak, little) that the author uses to emphasize what Abraham left behind
rejected: a little land and a feeble family and a small house
a small country and a weak family and a tiny home

choices.english: it was reckoned to him for righteousness
choices.why: Standard biblical idiom; keeps the passive of λογίζομαι and the prepositional phrase with εἰς
rejected: it was counted to him as righteousness

choices.term: πρὸς τὸ ὄρος ὃ ἔδειξεν αὐτῷ
choices.english: at the mountain which he showed him
choices.why: πρός with accusative here indicates place (at/near the mountain), not purpose; keeps the relative clause as restrictive
rejected: to the mountain which he showed him
on the mountain that he had shown him

pass_b_english: Abraham was called the friend of God, and he was found faithful because he obeyed the words of God.

Through obedience he left his own land, his relatives, and his father's house. He gave up a small land, a weak family, and a little house so that he might inherit the promises of God. For God says to him: "Go from your land and from your relatives and from your father's house to the land that I will show you. I will make you into a great nation, and I will bless you and make your name great, and you will be blessed. I will bless those who bless you and curse those who curse you, and in you all the tribes of the earth will be blessed" (Genesis 12:1-3).

Again, when Abraham was separated from Lot, God said to him: "Lift up your eyes and look from the place where you are now, toward the north and the south and the east and the sea, for all the land that you see I will give to you and to your descendants forever. And I will make your descendants like the sand of the earth; if anyone can count the sand of the earth, then your descendants also will be counted" (Genesis 13:14-16).

And again Scripture says: "God brought Abraham out and said to him: 'Look up to heaven and count the stars, if you are able to count them. So shall your descendants be.' And Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned to him for righteousness" (Genesis 15:5-6).
Because of faith and hospitality a son was given to him in old age, and through obedience he offered him as a sacrifice to God at the mountain which God showed him.

problems.source_quote: καὶ ποιήσω τὸ σπέρμα σου ὡς τὴν ἄμμον τῆς γῆς: εἰ δύναταί τις ἐξαριθμῆσαι τὴν ἄμμον τῆς γῆς, καὶ τὸ σπέρμα σου ἐξαριθμηθήσεται
problems.why: The 'sand of the earth' promise is Genesis 22:17, not 13:14-16; 13:16 has 'dust of the earth'.
problems.ruling: Source cites Gen 13:14-16 but includes sand promise (τὴν ἄμμον τῆς γῆς) from Gen 22:17; 13:16 says dust.

edits.old: And I will make your descendants like the sand of the earth; if anyone can count the sand of the earth, then your descendants also will be counted" (Genesis 13:14-16).
edits.new: And I will make your descendants like the sand of the earth; if anyone can count the sand of the earth, then your descendants also will be counted" (Genesis 13:14-15, 22:17).

fixed: The scripture citation was corrected to (Genesis 13:14-15, 22:17) because the sand promise is from Genesis 22:17, not 13:14-16.

problems.source_quote: καὶ ποιήσω τὸ σπέρμα σου ὡς τὴν ἄμμον τῆς γῆς: εἰ δύναταί τις ἐξαριθμῆσαι τὴν ἄμμον τῆς γῆς, καὶ τὸ σπέρμα σου ἐξαριθμηθήσεται
problems.why: The sand promise is Genesis 13:16 or 22:17, not 13:14-15. 13:14-15 lacks the sand simile; the citation conflates verses.

fixed: The sand promise is Genesis 13:16, so the citation has been corrected to (Genesis 13:14-16).

polish.changed: Clarified who speaks and when, made the sequence of Abraham's acts easier to follow, and kept every quotation and reference intact.

last_rejected.why: Glossary term φιλοξενία not used; 'hospitality' is not the fixed rendering.
last_rejected.fix: Because of faith and love of strangers a son was given to him in old age
last_rejected.ruling: φιλοξενίαν means 'hospitality'; rendering is within normal range. No glossary evidence provided.

last_rejected.source_quote: καὶ πάλιν ἐν τῷ διαχωρισθῆναι αὐτὸν ἀπὸ Λὼτ εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ θεός...καὶ ποιήσω τὸ σπέρμα σου ὡς τὴν ἄμμον τῆς γῆς
last_rejected.why: The sand promise is Genesis 13:16 only; verse 15 is missing from citation range. Should be 13:14-16 or 13:14-15.
last_rejected.ruling: Source quotes Gen 13:14-16 including sand promise; citation 13:14-16 is correct. Claim's own suggestion is confused.
